ingredients.cook_qty: 3 tbsp plus a drizzle for serving

instructions: Peel the potatoes and cut them into 1/2 inch cubes. Finely dice the onion and the celery, and mince the garlic. Grate the Parmesan.
Heat 3 tbsp of the olive oil in a large heavy pot over medium heat. Add the onion, the celery and 1/2 tsp of the salt. Cook, stirring now and then, until the onion is soft and clear, about 6 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds, until you can smell it. Push the vegetables to one side and add the tomato paste to the empty spot. Cook it for 1 minute, until it darkens to a brick red.
Pour in 1 cup of the broth and scrape up the browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Add the remaining 4 cups of broth, the potatoes, the remaining 1/2 tsp salt and the pepper.
Bring it to a boil, then turn the heat to medium-low, partly cover, and simmer until the potatoes are mostly tender, about 12 minutes.
Stir in the ditalini. Raise the heat so it bubbles steadily and cook for 5 minutes, stirring often so the ditalini doesn't stick to the bottom.
Take the pot off the heat, cover it, and leave it for 10 minutes. The ditalini will finish cooking and the soup will thicken to a creamy stew.
Stir in 1/3 cup of the Parmesan. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve in bowls with the rest of the Parmesan and a drizzle of olive oil.
To pack it for lunch, cool it and keep it in the fridge for up to 3 days. It thickens as it sits, so stir in a splash of water when you reheat it on the stove or in the microwave.
method_notes: Mangia with Michele (the lead, 5 out of 5 from 5 ratings, so below the 20 needed) builds the soup on a soffritto and tomato paste, with the potatoes cooked first and the pasta finished off the heat. Her pancetta, cheese rind and saffron are left out so the soup is vegetarian; olive oil and the grated cheese carry the flavor, and the broth supplies the depth. It takes about 50 minutes, so it is a big pot that makes several lunches, not a 30 minute lunch. It was the only readable version of this dish with any ratings, so there is no second source.
